whatChanged.title: AI stayed large but lost some internal share
whatChanged.detail: Coverage remained mainstream, yet adjacent infrastructure and automation themes took incremental attention inside technology-general.

whyItMatters.summary: AI can remain structurally important even while leadership rotates toward the infrastructure and deployment layers around it.
statements: The brief should distinguish mainstream persistence from fresh acceleration.
Softening share is not the same as decline if AI remains the dominant reference frame for adjacent themes.

requiredClaims: The theme should still rank among the highest-share technology children.
Brief language should mention rotation into semiconductors, cloud infrastructure, or robotics when present.
provenanceExpectations: Use aggregates for relative share, not only article count.
Future SEC evidence should clarify whether enterprise spend is broadening or concentrating.
notes: Avoid writing this brief as if AI disappeared just because attention diversified.

subtopicMovement.rationale: The space is mature enough that persistence matters more than raw novelty.
Operational deployment and cost efficiency remain strong adjacent signals.

pathways.note: Hyperscaler capex and enterprise distribution remain high-grade evidence.
Chip suppliers indicate whether AI demand remains infrastructure-heavy.

risks.title: Narrative saturation
risks.detail: A very large theme can create article-volume bias that looks like structural change when nothing new happened.

watchpoints.trigger: Capex and enterprise deployment commentary stays strong
watchpoints.implication: AI remains the backbone theme even if adjacent children gain share.

prompts: Is AI losing structural importance, or is value simply shifting to the infrastructure and adoption layers around it?

notes: This gold brief should stop the generator from confusing relative-share softening with thematic collapse.
